marques.title: One shared codebase serving radically different art directions
marques.lead: Each card pairs live Desktop (16:10) and Mobile (9:16) video captures of the deployed campaign with the brief’s creative challenge and the technical response provided by /base-vue-3.

contexte.title: Moving away from one-off builds for every campaign
contexte.lead: At Veepee Ad Studio, each brand campaign is a tailored event experience built on a tight schedule and localized across 13 European markets. Before /base-vue-3, four recurring bottlenecks slowed production.

architecture.title: Structuring a modular catalog of 32 self-contained components
architecture.lead: To end code duplication, we organized the repository around a clear contract: every component lives in its own directory with its template, TypeScript logic, SASS styles, type definitions, documentation, and layout variants.

thematisation.title: Rebranding every campaign through SASS variable overrides
thematisation.lead: Component source files contain no hardcoded brand values. All visual styling flows through a two-tier SASS variable layer and fluid unit functions (vw() on mobile, du() on desktop).

variants.title: Splitting the HeaderCus opening component into five isolated layouts
variants.lead: The opening hero concentrates most bespoke creative requests. Rather than piling conditional branches into a single file, HeaderCus isolates its five layout architectures (top, bottom, pop-in, block, center) in dedicated subfolders.

headerAnimation.title: Driving intro and scroll sequences through a declarative API
headerAnimation.lead: The HeaderCusAnimation sub-engine turns complex GSAP choreography into declarative configuration props (:animations="{ intro, scroll }"), synchronized with asset loading and legal consent.

catalogueGsap.title: Industrializing interactive and promotional campaign mechanics
catalogueGsap.lead: Beyond the opening hero, the entire user journey relies on seven configurable business components combining typed variant unions, scrubbed ScrollTriggers, and GSAP physics.

gouvernance.title: Maintaining continuous alignment across Figma, code, and documentation
gouvernance.lead: Leading both Figma design and Vue 3 engineering allowed me to enforce a strict 1:1 mapping between design components, SASS tokens, TypeScript contracts, and embedded documentation.

impact.title: Live production proofs and operational gains across Europe

rolePillars.text: UX/UI design in Figma of modular templates, opening sequences, and engagement mechanics (spinning wheel, instant win, scroll-stacked cards) serving both brand equity and conversion.
Two-tier SASS token architecture (global and per-component), 1:1 alignment between Figma variants and code subfolders, and video-illustrated Readme.md guides.
Vue 3, TypeScript, and GSAP architecture (timelineManager, scrollManager, Appear mixin, 8 custom directives), CLI scaffolding script (new_component.sh), Vue 2.7 to Vue 3 migration, and code reviews.

samsung.challenge: Showcase multiple high-tech product lines (TV, home appliances, mobile) with a full-screen video opening while preserving initial load speed.
samsung.resolution: Combined the HeaderCus (center) variant and lazy-loaded VideoCus player with MultiOffer and Sticky to keep conversion actions accessible throughout the scroll.

peugeot.challenge: Allow users to compare several car models and trim levels within a single event page without reloading.
peugeot.resolution: Two-way Vuex synchronization between the NavBar and the Slider carousel (5 variants), running on the Vue 3 and TypeScript foundation.

mms.challenge: Express a playful, colorful pop identity while preserving the structural rigor and accessibility of promotional offer blocks.
mms.resolution: Full rebranding through SASS token overrides (_variables.scss), HeaderCusAnimation opening sequence (imageAppear / textAppear), and staggered reveals via the Appear mixin.

pink-october.challenge: Rally the community around a multilingual international charity campaign built around an educational game mechanic.
pink-october.resolution: Built a custom Memory Card mini-game backed by Modal, Collect, and the 13-market multilingual architecture of /base-vue-3.

picard.challenge: Drive immediate promo-code redemption while showcasing a multi-category gourmet catalog.
picard.resolution: Embedded the CopyCode component (clipboard copy and GSAP visual feedback) inside Offer, paired with an editoCard Slider carousel.

coffee-b.challenge: Explain a product innovation (aluminum-free coffee ball) through progressive scroll storytelling before presenting the purchase offer.
coffee-b.resolution: Configured MultiOffer in Stacking mode (ScrollTrigger pinning with 3D perspective scale and brightness depth) to pace the product narrative.

pierre-vacances.challenge: Immerse visitors in a holiday atmosphere from the opening screen while keeping the promotional offer and destinations immediately visible.
pierre-vacances.resolution: Used the HeaderCus pop-in variant (floating card straddling the hero visual) animated by HeaderCusAnimation, followed by a synchronized destination carousel.

claudie-pierlot.challenge: Respect the understated editorial codes of premium ready-to-wear while integrating clear promotional mechanics.
claudie-pierlot.resolution: Paired the clean HeaderCus top variant with the lookbook Gallery grid (asymmetric column shift and scroll parallax) and a brand-tokenized CopyCode block.

fdj.challenge: Trigger an interactive GSAP opening sequence (animated star picker) only after the user clears the mandatory 18+ legal age gate.
fdj.resolution: Coordinated via timelineManager: the Consent modal pauses the master timeline until accepted, then releases the interactive intro and page scroll.

problems.label: 01 · Campaigns cloned from previous folders
problems.text: Each project started by duplicating a previous campaign directory, creating diverging codebases that were slow to review and expensive to maintain.

problems.label: 02 · Re-implemented business logic
problems.text: Consent modals, carousels, promo codes, video players, and Mixpanel tracking events were rewritten from one campaign to the next.

problems.label: 03 · Uncoordinated GSAP animations
problems.text: Opening animations sometimes fired behind the loading screen or legal modal, and ScrollTrigger measurements drifted on mobile viewports.

problems.label: 04 · Inconsistent quality across 13 markets
problems.text: Without TypeScript contracts or in-repo documentation, final rendering quality depended heavily on the assigned developer and schedule pressure.

veepee.quoteText: Our core objective: drastically cut campaign assembly time while giving every brand full freedom over its art direction and motion choreography.

architecture.problem: With more than 50 contributors across engineering, design, and delivery working on parallel campaigns, folder duplication created heavy technical debt and slowed onboarding.
architecture.decision: Separate the 19 atomic and cross-cutting components (src/components/) from the 13 configurable business blocks (_modulus/), require full co-location (.vue, .ts, .scss, Types.ts, Readme.md), and automate creation via scripts/new_component.sh.
architecture.resolution: A single shared foundation (/base-vue-3) maintained across two framework generations (Vue 2.7 then Vue 3), reducing campaign production time by 30–50%.

thematisation.problem: Serving visual identities as different as Claudie Pierlot, M&M’s, and Samsung with the exact same Vue components required a strict separation between DOM structure and visual styling.
thematisation.decision: Externalize all visual properties into a per-component _variables.scss file, convert dimensions into fluid units (vw() on mobile, du() on desktop), and introduce the v-brand directive.
thematisation.resolution: Adapting to a new brand happens entirely through SASS variable overrides and configuration files, without modifying component logic.

variants.role: Product Designer · System Designer · Lead Dev
variants.problem: The campaign hero (HeaderCus) concentrates the majority of custom creative requests: accumulating v-if branches inside a single file made it brittle on responsive layouts.
variants.decision: Define five reference layouts in Figma (top, bottom, pop-in, block, center) and isolate each variant in its own variants/<Name>/ subfolder with dedicated .vue, .ts, and .scss files.
variants.resolution: Switching layouts takes a single typed prop (variant="pop-in"), ensuring complete isolation between variants and exact parity with Figma.

headerAnimation.problem: GSAP intro sequences occasionally started before the Loader or legal Consent modal closed, and early scrolling threw off ScrollTrigger calculations.
headerAnimation.decision: Extract a dedicated engine (HeaderCusAnimation) driven by a declarative prop (:animations="{ intro, scroll }"), lock scrolling during the intro, and sequence everything in timelineManager.ts.
headerAnimation.resolution: A deterministic execution order (Loader → Consent → Header → HeaderAnimation → Sticky → Slider) unlocking 7 clip-path masks, 5 zoom curves, pinning, and progressive blur without imperative GSAP code.

catalogueGsap.role: Product Designer · System Designer · Lead Dev
catalogueGsap.problem: Campaign briefs regularly called for rich interactive mechanics (spinning wheel, 3D stacked cards, parallax lookbook, synchronized carousels) on schedules too short for custom builds.
catalogueGsap.decision: Engineer seven polymorphic business blocks with built-in GSAP timelines, scrubbed ScrollTriggers, and the cross-cutting Appear mixin.
catalogueGsap.resolution: Interactive mechanics once reserved for high-budget builds became reliable, accessible components activated through simple configuration.

gouvernance.role: Product Designer · System Designer · Lead Dev
gouvernance.problem: Documentation hosted outside the code repository (Notion or Confluence) quickly falls out of date during production peaks, creating gaps between Figma specs and shipped code.
gouvernance.decision: Mirror Figma naming in SASS tokens and variants/ folders, strictly type every prop in *Types.ts, and require a video-illustrated Readme.md guide inside every component directory.
gouvernance.resolution: 28 Readme.md guides versioned alongside source code, faster code reviews, and immediate autonomy for developers joining the team.

levers.title: A component API stable across two framework generations
levers.text: Prop contracts carried over from Vue 2.7 to Vue 3 (Vite and TypeScript) without disrupting the team’s integration workflow.

levers.title: SASS theming through simple variable overrides
levers.text: Every component exposes its tokens in _variables.scss and adapts to each brand’s guidelines without stylesheet duplication.

levers.title: CLI generator for standardized component creation
levers.text: The scripts/new_component.sh script scaffolds the complete directory (.vue, .ts, .scss, Types.ts, Readme.md) and registers SASS variables in one command.

variantDescs: Logo, main headline, and subtitle stacked at the top above the 16:9 panoramic visual.
Full-bleed visual at the top with editorial copy and call-to-action anchored at the bottom.
Floating card straddling the media with customizable drop shadow and corner radius.
Two-column structured layout separating the media from the promotional offer.
Full-screen centered composition over video or a clip-path animated slideshow.

headerAnimationPillars.label: 01 · Opening sequence
headerAnimationPillars.title: imageAppear + textAppear
headerAnimationPillars.text: Locks page scroll ($scroll.disableScroll()) during the opening choreography, paces headline, subtitle, offer, and CTA entrances with relative GSAP offsets ("-=0.4", ">"), then restores scrolling.

headerAnimationPillars.label: 02 · Visual transitions
headerAnimationPillars.title: 7 clip-path masks × 5 zooms
headerAnimationPillars.text: Animates desktop and mobile visual transitions using polygonal GSAP masks (left, right, up, down, sandwichX, sandwichY, random) paired with scale curves (zoom-in, zoom-out, zoom-pulse, zoom-rotate).

headerAnimationPillars.label: 03 · Continuous scroll scrub
headerAnimationPillars.title: pin, pinToElement, scaled, filtered
headerAnimationPillars.text: Pins the opening media on scroll up to any target selector (.app__container, .multi-offer, .footer-cus) while smoothly scrubbing scale (scaled: 1.15) or CSS filters (blur(8px), grayscale).

headerAnimationPillars.label: 04 · Global synchronization
headerAnimationPillars.title: Coordinated with Loader and Consent
headerAnimationPillars.text: Ensures no opening animation plays unseen in the background: readyTimeline waits for the Loader and Consent modal to close before running header → headerAnimation> → sticky> → slider.

gsapComponents.name: Cards
gsapFeatures: Scroll-triggered reveal via ScrollTrigger (autoAlpha + yPercent)
Dynamic badges (text or Icomoon icon)
Native support for ImgCus, VideoCus, and modal pop-ins
gsapComponents.problem: Each brand presented its products, categories, or trust signals with slightly different card layouts, spawning redundant components across projects.
gsapComponents.resolution: Consolidated into a single component with 5 typed variants, natively handling 2-column mobile grids (row), rounded badges (stickersRounded), star ratings (Rating), video, and staggered scroll reveals.
gsapComponents.usedIn: Samsung, Peugeot, Claudie Pierlot, M&M’s, Picard, Pink October

gsapComponents.name: Slider
gsapFeatures: GSAP slideUp / slideDown entrance aligned with the slider timeline label
Two-way binding between Swiper 11 and the NavBar component
Focus mode with active slide scaling
gsapComponents.problem: On catalog-heavy campaigns (automotive, resorts, gourmet food), users easily lost track of the connection between the category navigation bar and the content carousel.
gsapComponents.resolution: Two-way Vuex synchronization between Swiper 11 and NavBar (swiping updates the active tab; clicking a tab triggers slideToLoop), paired with a coordinated GSAP entrance.

gsapComponents.name: MultiOffer (Stacking mode)
gsapFeatures: ScrollTrigger pin: true, scrub: 1, end: "+=200%"
Progressive vertical card overlap on scroll
3D depth effect combining scale and brightness() reduction
gsapComponents.problem: Stacking three or four promotional offers vertically made mobile pages overly long and caused user attention to drop before the final offer.
gsapComponents.resolution: Engineered Stacking.ts: the section pins on scroll while each incoming offer card slides over the previous one, which recedes in perspective and dims progressively.

gsapComponents.name: Collect (SpinningWheel mode)
gsapFeatures: GSAP Power4.easeOut rotation (5 full turns + target safeZone angle)
Real-time angular peg detection inside onUpdate()
Physical clapper animation (indicatorTl) and ScrollTrigger.refresh()
gsapComponents.problem: On lead-generation campaigns, standard forms converted poorly, yet building a smooth, deterministic prize wheel for each operation took too long.
gsapComponents.resolution: Integrated SpinningWheel into Collect: target stop-angle calculation (safeZone), 5-turn Power4.easeOut spin, and realistic clapper bounce triggered in onUpdate as each peg passes.
gsapComponents.usedIn: Pink October and gamified brand campaigns

gsapComponents.name: Gallery
gsapFeatures: shifted: asymmetric vertical column offset on scroll
parallax: internal image counter-translation inside its frame
Automatic height compensation when the .sticky bar is active
gsapComponents.problem: Fashion and ready-to-wear brands wanted an editorial magazine lookbook feel on scroll rather than a static product grid.
gsapComponents.resolution: Built the Gallery component combining three ScrollTrigger effects (shifted, parallax, animate) into 8 possible configurations, with automatic offset recalculation when a Sticky bar is present.

gsapComponents.name: Sticky
gsapFeatures: Dual ScrollTrigger: entry appearance point and bottom exit point
Automatic deactivation before FooterCus or a custom target selector
Appearance synchronized with the sticky> milestone in timelineManager
gsapComponents.problem: A floating bottom CTA improves conversion, but clutters the opening Hero on load and covers mandatory legal notices at the bottom of the page.
gsapComponents.resolution: Driven by a dual ScrollTrigger: the bar only appears once the opening sequence completes (sticky> milestone) and automatically retracts as soon as the footer enters the viewport.

gsapComponents.name: Offer (with Appear Mixin)
gsapFeatures: Timer component with scroll-driven compact mode (timerShrink)
CopyCode component with GSAP visual confirmation on click
Cross-cutting appear mixin (boolean | object | array) and appearChildren
gsapComponents.problem: Promotional mechanics (countdown timer, copyable promo code, voucher, dual offer) were repeatedly recoded with inconsistent behaviors and entrance animations.
gsapComponents.resolution: Centralized these mechanics inside the Offer block and created the Appear mixin, enabling entrance animations on any component or its child elements via a single prop.
gsapComponents.usedIn: Pierre & Vacances, Claudie Pierlot, Picard, M&M’s, FDJ

rules.text: Every component directory includes its Readme.md guide detailing prop contracts, usage examples, and video captures of animated states.

rules.text: Each layout variant lives in its own variants/ subfolder with dedicated .vue, .ts, and .scss files to prevent monolithic components.

proofNotes.fdj: Interactive GSAP intro (star picker) · Demo environment

impact.label: 30 to 50% faster delivery
impact.text: A standard campaign is assembled through component composition and SASS variable overrides; engineering time goes into art direction and custom animations.

impact.label: Reliable motion and core features
impact.text: Consent management, loader, GSAP orchestration (timelineManager), fluid responsive units (vw/du), and Mixpanel tracking are inherited automatically.

impact.label: Rollout across 13 European markets
impact.text: Launching a campaign in a new country or for a new brand only requires i18n configuration files and SASS tokens.

learnings: Handling Figma design, Design System architecture, and Vue/GSAP engineering together removes information loss between design intent and production.
Versioning documentation and demo videos directly inside each component folder is the most reliable way to keep them accurate over time.
Decoupling layout structure (HeaderCus) from the declarative animation engine (HeaderCusAnimation and timelineManager) enables bespoke creative campaigns on a stable industrial foundation.

meta.description: Design System Case Study: 6-layer unidirectional architecture, single-source tokens, orchestrated GSAP motion, 9 automated quality gates, and interactive Storybook.

hero.eyebrow: Case Study 02 · Front-End Architecture · CI Governance
hero.titlePrefix: A Design System built from the ground up,
hero.leadPrefix: Building on the lessons learned from
hero.leadSuffix: at Veepee, I designed this architecture for the rebuild of an editorial media platform — and reused it directly to build this portfolio. The goal: turn every design and architectural convention into a blocking verification script.
badges: Lead Dev · System Designer · Product Designer

contexte.title: Building a fast editorial platform without letting the architecture drift
contexte.lead: The media platform rebuild had to meet three strict engineering requirements from sprint one: instant perceived navigation, page assembly driven by a headless CMS, and a codebase able to scale without losing consistency.

architecture.title: Six layers with strictly unidirectional dependencies
architecture.lead: The source tree separates four component pillars (core, ui, blocks, domains) from two assembly and routing layers (layouts, pages). Import direction is automatically verified on every commit.

motion.title: Orchestrating five GSAP engines without content flashes or rendering conflicts
motion.lead: All animations across the media platform and this portfolio are centralized in src/core/motion/: pre-paint preparation, section pinning, accessible typographic splitting, and row-by-row grid reveals.

gardefous.title: Nine blocking quality gates unified under a single command
gardefous.lead: So quality never depends on code-review vigilance alone, every change runs through a complete static analysis, type-checking, and architectural validation pipeline.

workflow.title: Structuring release flow, technical specifications, and security

storybook.title: Making Storybook the visual and accessibility reference for the project
storybook.lead: Every primitive, composition block, and domain component is built in isolation, documented, and audited against WCAG 2.1 AA criteria. The Storybook compiled alongside this portfolio exposes all 25 of these components online.

labels.tokensExcerptLabel: tokens.css — excerpt from the single source of truth

kpis.label: component pillars
kpis.note: core · ui · blocks · domains (+ layouts, pages)

kpis.label: atomic UI primitives
kpis.note: src/ui/ · ported from the media platform

contexte.role: From Veepee (/base-vue-3) field lessons to CI automation
contexte.problem: On /base-vue-3 at Veepee, enforcing conventions partly relied on our vigilance during code reviews. When delivery pace accelerates, any rule not verified by tooling eventually gets bypassed.
contexte.decision: Formalize every architecture, design token, theme, and co-location rule at the root of the repository and pair it with a blocking check script.
contexte.resolution: Architectural or styling deviations are caught locally by npm run check before a Pull Request is even opened.

architecture.problem: In many front-end codebases, src/components/ ends up mixing UI primitives, CMS schemas, and business logic, making clean reuse impossible.
architecture.decision: Structure src/ into 6 layers with a strict unidirectional flow (core → ui → blocks → domains → layouts → pages) and ban cross-dependencies between business domains.
architecture.resolution: This portfolio demonstrates that portability firsthand: it reuses the exact core, ui, blocks, and layouts layers from the media platform while swapping only the business domains (work, about, navigation).

principes.problem: Gradually introducing hardcoded values (hex colors, pixel sizes, one-off shadows) quickly erodes typographic and thematic consistency across an interface.
principes.decision: Centralize all visual decisions in src/core/styles/tokens.css (colors, fluid clamp() type scale, easing curves, paper grain) and verify the absence of hardcoded values via lint:tokens.
principes.resolution: Updating the visual identity happens in a single file (tokens.css) and every themed section guarantees contrast parity through its data-theme attribute.

motion.problem: On a multi-page architecture with hydrated islands (Astro and Svelte 5), triggering separate entrance and scroll animations on the same element causes visual jumps and transform conflicts.
motion.decision: Consolidate the entire lifecycle in AnimationOrchestrator (pre-paint preparation under data-anim-pending, strict 'one element = one animation event' rule) and measure grids on their static geometry.
motion.resolution: Five coordinated 60fps GSAP engines (SectionTimelines, accessible TextSplitter, row-based StaggeredGrids, data-stack pinning, and vector borders) natively honoring prefers-reduced-motion.

gardefous.problem: An external best-practices document cannot prevent a circular import, a TypeScript any, a hardcoded color, or an unused export from slipping in under deadline pressure.
gardefous.decision: Combine nine complementary tools (astro check, svelte-check, ESLint, Stylelint, lint:tokens, lint:themes, lint:arch, Knip, and Prettier) under the single npm run check command.
gardefous.resolution: Full validation completes in seconds, letting code reviews focus on functional relevance and user experience.

workflow.problem: Scaling contributors on a shared front-end repository quickly exposes the project to merge conflicts, silent regressions, and a hard-to-audit Git history.
workflow.decision: Codify normative rules in AGENTS.md at the repository root and enforce a structured release flow (feat/* → alpha → main) gated by npm run check and npm run build.
workflow.resolution: Every production release is isolated, tagged semantically, and verified across accessibility, performance, and security.

storybook.problem: Testing a component only inside a full page misses content edge cases, contrast issues, or keyboard navigation flaws.
storybook.decision: Require a <Name>.stories.ts file in every UI, Block, and Domain component directory (enforced by lint:arch), generate Svelte 5 Autodocs, and enable automated WCAG 2.1 AA auditing (addon-a11y).
storybook.resolution: 70 interactive stories, 27 documentation pages, and 9 play interaction tests are compiled alongside the site (/storybook/index.html), inspectable in French or English across 4 viewports and 3 themed surfaces.

constraints.label: Requirement 01 · Performance
constraints.title: Instant rendering and smooth transitions
constraints.text: Server-side rendering (SSR), selective Svelte 5 island hydration, hover link prefetching, and pre-paint motion preparation.

constraints.label: Requirement 02 · Editorial Scalability
constraints.title: Schema-driven page assembly
constraints.text: Automated TypeScript generation from the CMS schema, strict JSON dictionary internationalization, and pages composed from generic blocks.

constraints.label: Requirement 03 · Maintainability
constraints.title: Protection against architectural drift
constraints.text: Strict boundaries between technical layers, ban on magic values, and mechanical verification of component contracts on every commit.

pillars.title: Cross-cutting foundation
pillars.text: Design tokens (tokens.css), global styles, GSAP orchestrator, procedural paper-grain texture (2D Domain-Warped fBm injected via adoptedStyleSheets with zero scroll cost), i18n, and utilities.

pillars.text: 10 UI primitives in this repository (ported from the 25 foundational primitives of the media platform): button, badge, heading, media, video, code block, accordion, counter… Each directory groups its Svelte component, CSS, and stories.

pillars.title: Composition blocks
pillars.text: 8 reusable editorial blocks (ported from the 12 blocks of the media platform): section header, asymmetric split, bento grid, quote, key stats, component tree, Case Study summary, and timeline.

ESLint: bans any types and unused variables across Astro, Svelte, and TypeScript.

principles.label: Unidirectional dependency flow
principles.text: core → ui → blocks → domains → layouts → pages. A lower layer never imports a module from a higher layer.

principles.label: Tokens as the single source of truth
principles.text: All colors, shadows, easing curves, and fluid clamp() typographic scales come exclusively from tokens.css.

principles.label: Full folder co-location
principles.text: Each component groups its markup, stylesheet, Storybook stories, and types in a single directory, without barrel index.ts files.

principles.label: Routes dedicated to HTTP routing
principles.text: Files in src/pages/ only resolve the locale and invoke the matching page template in under 60 lines.

principles.label: Automated section theme parity
principles.text: Every section with a themed background carries the matching data-theme attribute, verified by lint:themes.

principles.label: Mobile-First engineering
principles.text: Base styles target mobile screens with progressive enhancements from 768px up and a centralized header height token.

workflow.title: Branch promotion flow
workflow.text: The main branch (production) is promoted from alpha via fast-forward merge and semantic tag after staging validation on pre-alpha.

workflow.title: Isolated feature branches
workflow.text: Each change (feat/* or fix/*) branches from alpha, passes npm run check and npm run build, and merges with --no-ff.

workflow.title: Versioned normative rules
workflow.text: Architecture and component contracts are documented in AGENTS.md at the repository root and enforced identically locally and in CI.

workflow.title: Comprehensive technical specs
workflow.text: The system jointly covers GSAP choreography, data typing, and security hardening (XSS/SSRF sanitization, CSP and HSTS headers).

storybookFacts.title: Structure mirroring the codebase
storybookFacts.text: The Foundations, UI, Blocks, and Domains navigation mirrors the exact organization of src/.

storybookFacts.title: Built-in accessibility auditing
storybookFacts.text: The a11y addon evaluates every component against WCAG 2.1 AA criteria directly inside the workbench.

storybookFacts.title: Four calibrated viewports
storybookFacts.text: Mobile (375px), tablet (768px), laptop (1280px), and desktop (1440px) match the system’s breakpoints.

storybookFacts.title: Multi-theme and bilingual previewing
storybookFacts.text: Every story can be inspected in French or English (FR / EN) across dark, raised, and surface themed backgrounds to validate contrast.

motionEngines.title: Lifecycle orchestrator (AnimationOrchestrator)
motionEngines.text: Manages Astro ClientRouter transitions: pre-paint hiding under data-anim-pending, timed #global-loader bar (>120ms), outro fade, and coordinated first-wave launch.

motionEngines.title: Accessible typographic splitting (SectionTimeline)
motionEngines.text: Splits headings into masked lines (yPercent 118 → 0) while preserving screen-reader accessibility (aria-label) and CSS gradients on <em> tags.

motionEngines.title: Row-by-row grid reveal (StaggeredGrid)
motionEngines.text: Dynamically groups cards by their static vertical position (offsetTop) so each visual row triggers its own ScrollTrigger.

motionEngines.title: Depth section pinning (Stacking)
motionEngines.text: Pins key sections (data-stack) while the following section slides over with progressive recession (scale: 0.92 and dimming), and handles footer reveal.

motionEngines.title: Scroll parallax and SVG stroke drawing
motionEngines.text: Applies smooth vertical translation on [data-parallax] elements and animates vector perimeter strokes (stroke-dashoffset) on buttons.

faq.title: Why strictly isolate business domains?
faq.content: Each business domain evolves, is tested, and can be replaced without impacting the rest of the system. That is what made it possible to move from the media platform (articles, agenda, engagement) to this portfolio (work, about, navigation) while keeping core, ui, and blocks untouched.

faq.title: Why keep all design tokens in a single file?
faq.content: Adapting the system to a new visual identity only requires updating tokens.css. This portfolio uses the exact same primitives and composition blocks as the original media platform.

faq.title: How do you ensure these rules hold over time?
faq.content: Conventions are documented in AGENTS.md at the root of the repository and each one is enforced by a dedicated script inside npm run check before every merge.
